estimates.notes: The PDF prints both arm SDs as "SD = 08", with no decimal point. The numeric SD fields are null because the intended value cannot be confirmed without correcting the paper; the exact printing is retained in the source quote. The reported 95% CI [.021, .045] follows t, p, and d without identifying its target; its bounds are transcribed in stats.ci_lower and stats.ci_upper, with ci_of null. It is not assigned to d. No mean difference, SE, SD of paired differences, or within-person outcome correlation is printed. No quantities were calculated. The unit and SD level are participant because each person contributes one story in each condition. The reported paired t-test treats people as the analysis units. Figure 2 on PDF p. 15 shows confidence-interval error bars without numeric endpoints; no numbers were read from the plot. Only the full-sample paired contrast is reported; no first-round or order-specific contrast is available.

estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: Leave-one-out contribution of each story to its prompt-specific dataset: the dataset mean of all pairwise semantic distances (1 minus cosine similarity), minus the same mean with that story removed. Uses final-layer sentence embeddings from paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2; prompt words are removed before embedding. Datasets are split by writing prompt rather than condition. Positive scores mean the story adds diversity. Methods: PDF pp. 11-12; Figure 1, PDF p. 13. One contribution score per participant per condition.

estimates.notes: Means, SDs, and the reported CI are retained in the units printed in the Results. Figure 2 (PDF p. 15) multiplies diversity contribution by 10^3 only for plotting; no conversion was applied and no numeric CI endpoints were read from that figure. The reported 95% CI [-0.0001, -0.0000006] follows t, p, and d without identifying its target; ci_of is null and these bounds are not assigned to d. Both arm levels are mean per-story contributions to prompt-specific reference pools. Because prompts were counterbalanced across conditions (PDF p. 9) and the diversity datasets were split by prompt only (PDF pp. 11-12), the reference pools mix conditions; this is an inference from the stated method. The paper does not report separate within-arm set diversity. Higher scores mean more diverse output. The negative reported contrast indicates lower diversity contributions with AI. The reported uncertainty is a paired t-test across participants, not a test treating all story pairs as independent. Each participant contributes one score per condition, although scores share reference pools; no adjustment for that shared-pool dependence is described. No numeric mean difference, SE, paired-difference SD, or within-person outcome correlation is printed. PDF p. 8 identifies this as a main outcome. Only the full-sample paired contrast is available; no first-round or order-specific contrast is reported.

open_items: Originality arm SDs require confirmation: the PDF literally prints "08" for both, so both numeric SD fields are null (PDF p. 14). No SD was computed from participant data.

For both eligible contrasts, the paper does not identify the estimand of its printed confidence interval or the standardizer used for d. ci_of is null; no paired-difference SD, within-person correlation, or SE is printed (PDF pp. 14 and 17).
The paper reports recruitment, not a count explicitly randomized to each condition order. Counts at assignment, analyzed counts by order, and exclusions by order remain unavailable (PDF pp. 8-9).

No first-round-only results or order/carryover analysis are reported. All participants had a practice story with ChatGPT available before both main conditions; actual practice use by every person is unstated (PDF pp. 9-11).
The diversity outcome uses prompt-specific pools that mix conditions; within-arm set diversity is not reported (PDF pp. 11-12).
The paper does not state a release year or exact API snapshot for its GPT 3.5 base model; ai_tool.year is null (PDF p. 10).
notes: Reconciled on 2026-10-09. The complete markdown conversion was read in consecutive chunks through the references and Appendices A-D. Every cited c159 PDF page was independently read with pymupdf; rendered pages were also inspected for the malformed originality SDs, the diversity definition, Figure 2, and the Appendix A/B interfaces. The PDF has no printed page numbers, so locators use PDF file page order. Both eligible screening-form outcomes and their sole reported full-sample AI-help versus No-AI contrasts are retained. S1-O3 is excluded as self-assessment, and all other skipped measures/analyses are listed in not_extracted. There are no estimates unique to A or B after matching the diversity records by outcome and contrast; no eligible estimate missed by both was found. Agreement was independently checked for the study and arm counts and for both estimates’ counts, question, construct, unit, higher_is, outcome_with_ai, and within_person. PDF p. 8 states that the study was online and recruited 391 students; PDF p. 9 explicitly reports a final sample of 263 and randomized condition order. Recruitment is not substituted for a printed randomized count, and people are not double-counted across conditions. The exclusions for external aid, attention checks, and cognitive-test performance precede the final sample statement; the later outlier exclusions apply only to the excluded prompt-count correlations (PDF pp. 8-9 and 15-17). The university’s country is supported by PDF p. 1. Shared-sample information is carried from forms/c159.json, sample_overlap, as instructed; the later c475 reanalysis is not independently established by c159 itself. No first-round-only or order/carryover analysis is printed. The practice story made ChatGPT available before both main conditions, but actual practice use by every participant is unstated (PDF pp. 10-11); no distinct after_ai contrast is reported. No estimates were calculated from raw data, figures, or formulas. The resolutions include both script-flagged fields and additional field differences found by directly comparing the two extraction files, including descriptive wording, p-value formatting, the diversity slug, and originality sd_level. Literal number formatting is retained in the source quotes even where JSON uses scientific notation.
